_note: Acme Freight Services — a third company, onboarded as DATA ONLY. There is no Python module for this pack and no entry in registry.PACK_MODULES; it exists to prove that the declarative work met its goal, and it is the test that fails if a future change makes a pack need code again. See tests/packs/test_datapack.py. This is a SYNTHETIC pack: it ships with no gold documents and no real corpus, so its constants are illustrative rather than measured, which is stated here rather than left for a reader to discover.
name: acme_freight

claim._why: An AP department, so the guard is the bill-to — the same shape as Northstar. Both markers name the company itself; neither is a bare address, so no corroboration tier is needed. The ship-to veto is carried over for the same reason it exists there: a freight company's own address routinely appears on documents billed to somebody else.

rungs.name: credit_memo_title
rungs._why: A genuine TITLE near the top of page 1, not a mention. Uses the same primitive and the same two constraints as Northstar's rung, which exists because real OCR wraps a footnote reference onto short lines that read exactly like a title.

rungs.name: statement_title_no_table
rungs._why: A document with a payable amount and line items is a bill whatever its header says, so the charges table has to be ABSENT. Presence of the word is never enough — that rule cost the Digital Direction pack $20,123.80 before it was learned.

tags._why: A standalone banner on a short line, never the phrase inside prose — every freight vendor prints past-due language in its terms and conditions.
Summit bills under two printed names. The tag makes the alias collapse visible on the record rather than a silent normalization nobody can audit.
